Attestation verification now compares user-supplied values literally when it builds the certificate subject pattern. Both edits are in `pkg/cmd/attestation/verify/policy.go`; I have not compiled it or run any tests.

- **Owner / repo / signer repo:** the full GitHub URL (host plus owner or repo) is regex-escaped before the `(?i)^…/` pattern is built. Host matching stays case-insensitive and the match still has to end at a `/`. A signer repo of `my.org/my.repo` no longer matches `myXorg/myXrepo`.
- **Signer workflow:** the whole workflow value is escaped, whether it includes a host or not. The explicit-host case and the default-hostname case are both covered. Dots in hosts and workflow file names stay literal, so legitimate dotted names (including GitHub Enterprise hosts) still match themselves.

Any existing test that asserts the exact unescaped regex strings (for example `^https://github.com/...`) will need updating to the escaped form. I couldn't see the tests, so I haven't checked.
